elements.text: 3. REQUIREMENTS

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: First article. When specified (see 6.2), a sample shall be subjected to first article inspection in accordance with 4.2.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Recycled, recovered or enviromnentally preferable materials. Recycled, recovered, or enviromnentally preferable materials should be used to the maximum extent possible, provided that the material meets or exceeds the operational and maintenance requirements, and promotes economically advantageous life cycle costs.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 3.3 Materials.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Basic material (Type n. The basic material for the Type I trousers shall be a 50/50% nylonlcotton ripstop blend, wind resistant poplin cloth in a universal camouflage pattern conforming to Class 8 ofMIL-DTL-44436.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Basic material (Type II) The basic material for the Type II trouser shall be a 65/25/1 0 flame resistant rayonlpara-aramidlnylon blend, cloth in universal camouflage pattern conforming to GLIPD 07-12.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Cloth, side and hip hanging pockets, and waistband lining (Type I and Type Il). The cloth for waistband lining, side and hip pockets, shall be basic material or ground shade cloth or printed UCP seconds. For printed material, prior to overprinting of the Universal Camouflage Pattern (UCP), the ground shade cloth for Type I shall be dyed conforming to class 6 ofMIL-DTL 44436 and for Type II shall be Desert Sand 500 in accordance with GL-PD 07-12. The ground shade (Type I and II) shall meet the respective finished fabric physical, mechanical, and dimensional requirements. Seconds shall be cloth which has been rejected only for defects pertaining to color, infrared reflectance, or camouflage printed pattern as specified in MIL-DTL44436 (Type I) or GL-PD 07-12 (Type II) as applicable.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Alternate side and hip hanging pockets (Type Ionly), As an alternate for Type I trouser only, a 5.04 ozlsq. yd. minimum, plain weave, 75% polyester 25% cotton, material or equal may be used for side and hip hanging pockets only. The color for the material shall be Desert Sand 500, Urban Grey 501, or Foliage Green 502. (See 6.4)

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: GLlPD 07-l4A

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.3.2.2 Alternate Flame Resistant (FR) side and hip hanging pockets (Type II only). As an alternate for Type II trouser, the following material type may be used for side and hip hanging pockets only, 7.0 to 8.0 ozlsq. yd., 2xlleft hand twill, with 91 x 47 warp/filling ends per inch (minimum), 80% cotton/20% meta aramid fiber blend. The material shall have the following flame resistance characteristics: After Flame of2.0 seconds (minimum); After Glow of25.0 seconds (maximum) and Char Length of 4.5 inches (maximum) initially and after 25 laundering cycles. The color for the material shall be Desert Sand 500, Urban Grey 50 I, or Foliage Green 502. (See 6.4.) Testing shall be as specified in 4.4.2. (See 6.4.1)

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.4 Insect bite protection. The Class 2 trouser shall be treated for insect bite protection. The finished trouser with bite protection treatment shall be sttictly limited to the level specified in 3.4.1 and provide the minimum insect bite protection specified in 3.4.2.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.4.1 Pelmethrin treatment (Class 2 only). Permethrin treatment process and gannents will comply with Federal Insecticide, Fungicide and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) as amended (see 2.2.2). Permethrin concentration in Class 2 trousers shall comply with EPA Toxological Category IV. The Class 2 trouser shall have an EPA registered (See 6.5) permethrin insect protection treatment which shall use pennethrin in accordance with Type II specified in MIL-DTL-444 1 1 except that the application for Type II specified in paragraph 3.5 (Labels and labeling)of MIL-DTL-444 1 1 shall also be applicable to finished garment. The trouser shall be labeled in accordance with 3.8.2.1.1 and 3.8.2.1.2. The pelmethrin finish shall be unifOlmly applied across the fabric or galment and strictly controlled to fall within the initial minimum to maximum pelmethrin levels specified below. The treatment level shall provide the percent (%) bite protection specified in 3.4.2. The permethrin treatment shall be durable to repeated laundeting. The pelmethrin level testing shall be as specified 4.4.2. The finished permethrin treatment shall not degrade any performance characteristics ofthe gmment or present any latent defects to the cloth or garment.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 3.5 Components.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 3.5.1 Tape and cord

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Barrel lock and hem tane (drawstring). The tape for the barrel lock and leg bottom hem shall conform to MIL-PRF-5038, Type III, 3/8 inch wide. The tape for attaching the barrel lock shall be cut approximately 2 inches in length so that when folded it finishes 3/4 (± 118) inch in length. The drawstring tape for the leg bottom hem shall be 32 (± I) inches in length. The tape ends shall be heat cut to prevent raveling and the ends of the bottom hem drawstring tape shall be finished with knotted ends. The color shall match Foliage Green 504.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Tape, FR identification marker (Type II trouser only). The tape for the FR identification marker shall be I-inch wide conforming to Type III ofMIL-PRF-5038. The tape ends shall be heat cut to prevent raveling. The color shall match Foliage Green 504.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Cord, elastic (drawcord). The elastic cord for the cargo pockets shall have a 118 (+ 1132, -0) inch diameter. The elastic cord properties shall be as follows: weight 0.20 oz.!linear yard, elongation 120 (± 10) percent, 55 picks/inch minimum, 16 caniers, 3 ends/carrier, 12 elastic strands minimum and polyester cover yam (see 6.4). The cord length shall be 14 (± 3/4) inches and shall be heat cut and have knotted ends. The color shall match Foliage Green 504. Testing shall be as specified in 4.4.2. (See 6.6.)

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Braid, flat tubular (drawstting). The flat tubular braided drawstting for the internal waistband shall conform to the following requirements: 1000 denier textured nylon cover yam, basket weave braid construction, II picks/inch minimum, 44 caniers, I-end per/carrier, 3/8 (± 1132) inch in width, and a 400 pounds break strength. The finished cut lengths shall have a tolerance of(± I inch) as follows: 50 inches for X-Small and Small; 52 inches for Medium and Large; and 54 inches for X-Large and XX-Large. The lengths shall be heat cut to prevent raveling and have knotted ends. The color shall be Foliage Green 504. Testing shall be as specified in 4.4.2

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Barrel lock. The barrel locks shall maintain a 3-pound minimum holding strength on elastic cord (see 3.5.3.3) when tested in accordance with 4.4.2. The ban'ellock shall be I12-inch x 3/8-inch elliptical or 3/8-inch round shape, push-button size to easily operate with gloves. The color shall match Foliage Green 504. Barrel lock shall be set for customer use before packaging. (See 6.7.)

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Fastener tape, hook and loop. The hook fastener tape shall conform to Type II, Class I or Type III, Class 4 and the loop fastener tape shall conform to Class I or Class 4 of A-A-55126. Hook and loop with slit, split edges or any splicing of fastener tape is not permitted. The widths shall be as specified for each application throughout this specification. The tolerance for all widths specified shall be (± 1/32) inch so as to prevent stitching runoffs or improper fit into

elements.label: text
elements.text: automatic sewing equipment. The color shall match Foliage Green 504. The fastener tape hook and loop Type and Class shall be consistent (same manufacturer/lot) within a garment. (See 6.8.)

elements.text: 3.5.5.2 Gimp. The cotton gimp for reinforcing buttonholes shall conform to A-A-50198, soft or glazed finish, Tex Size 180 or 210. The color shall match Foliage Green 504.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.5.6 Buttons. Buttons shall be dull finish, 4 holes, 30 ligne conforming to V-B-871, Type II, Class D, Style 26. The color shall match Foliage Green 504. When attached to the trouser, the button and thread shall withstand 40 Ibs (minimum) when tested as specified in 4.4.2.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.6 Design. The trousers shall have a waistband with clean finished ends with seven (7) belt loops, a drawstring and buttonlbuttonhole closure. The trousers shall have a covered fly with three (3) buttons and buttonhole closure. The trousers shall have two (2) side hanging pockets, two (2) back single welt hip pockets with two (2) button closure flaps, two (2) front side pleated cargo pockets with hook and loop closure flaps and two (2) lower leg pockets with hook and loop closure flaps. The front side cargo pockets shall have an elastic drawcord with barrel locks at the top hem. Both fi-ont side cargo pockets and lower leg pocket shall have sewn-in eyelets at the bottom of the bellows. The trousers shall have a double needle seat patch, and a knee patch on each leg with hook and loop closure at bottom and a drawstring at each leg bottom (see 3.5.1.1).

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.7 Constmction. All material edges shall be clean finished, either, turned-in, turned-under or serged unless otherwise indicated.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.7.1 Fastener tape, (hook and loop). All widths of hook and loop tape shall be sewn 1183/16 inch from bound selvage (for fastener tape with selvage) or from tape edge (for fastener tape without selvage) to prevent needle cutting along edges, stitching runoffs or improper fit into automatic sewing equipment. To prevent raveling on fastener tape with selvage, do not sew directly on the selvage. The use of fastener tape that is slit, has split edges, or any splicing of fastener tape is not permitted. Under no circumstances shall any fastener tape be re-stitched for repair purposes. New tape shall be used for repairs to prevent needle cutting, thus offering maximum field life. All fastener tape maybe sewn through all layers on trouser as indicated on the figures (see pattel11s for placement). Tolerance for all lengths offastener tape shall be ± 118 inch.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.7.2 Waistband. The finished waistband shall measure 1-3/4 (± 118) inches wide with clean finished ends and a buttonlbuttonhole closure. The width ofthe waistband shall be consistent so that the light and left sides match each other in width at the front within 3/16 inch. The waistband also has a flat tubular braided drawstring inserted through 112 inch straight cut vertical buttonholes or 3/8 inch sewn eyelets, with knotted ends for waist adjustment. The drawstring buttonholes or sewn eyelets shall be centered 3 (± 112) inches from finished edge on each side of waistband, and shall be of sufficient size and form as to allow the drawstring to move smoothly and evenly through the holes. The waistband shall also have a button and horizontal buttonhole closure that shall align vertically with the fly button and buttonhole closure (see figure 6).

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.7.3 Belt loops. The trouser shall have seven (7) belt loops measuring 3/8 - 112 inch in width and finish 2 - 2-1/4 inches between bartacks in the length. The belt loop placement shall be as follows: one (I) loop on each side seam, one (1) on back seam, and one (1) on each front centered between side seam and waistband end, and one (I) on each back side centered between side seam and back seam. Belt loops may be positioned immediately adjacent to felled seams to reduce bulk in sewing.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.7.4 Fly. The trouser fly shall be a covered fly with three (3) buttons and buttonhole closure. The buttonholes shall be horizontal and placed as indicated on the pattel11. The fly shall have "J" stitching 2-inches from fly edge. The top fly shall be edge stitched 1116 - 118 inch. See figure 6.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.7.5 Seat patch. The trouser shall have a double-needle seat patch (see pattel11 for placement). See figure 2.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.7.6 Knee patches. The trouser shall have a knee patch on each leg, for foam inserts, with an opening on the bottom with hook and loop closure. The top of the knee patch shall be double­ needle stitched. The opening shall be a minimum of 6 inches wide between bartacks and the channels shall be a minimum of 6 inches wide. The hook and loop tape for the closure shall be 5/8 inch wide by 6-112 inches long. Openings on each side ofthe knee patch hook and loop closure shall be top stitched closed prior to bartacking. The hook fastener shall be sewn on the underside of patch and the loop fastener on the trouser leg front. The hook and loop fastener tape shall be sewn on prior to finishing the knee patch assembly.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.7.7 Pockets and flaps.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Front side pockets. The trouser shall have two (2) front side hanging pockets with pocket openings measuring not less than 6 inches and not more than 7-114 inches between bartacks. Pocket openings shall match each other within 114 inch.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Hip pockets. The trousers shall have back left and right single welt hip pockets with a two (2) buttonlbuttonhole closure per pocket. The welt shall measure 3/16 - 112 inch. The buttons shall be sewn onto the outside of the pocket and the buttonholes shall be sewn into the underside of the flap as indicated on pattems.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Cargo pockets and flaps. The trouser shall have two (2) pleated bellows cargo pockets with flaps (see pattem for placement). The pockets shall have a sewn-in eyelet at the bottom of bellow, as indicated on the pattem (see 3.7.10). The pockets shall have an elastic drawcord (see 3.5.1.3) inserted through eyelets at the top of pocket hem with a barrel lock (see 3.5.3) for adjustment. The ban'ellock shall be attached to the side of the cargo pocket with a piece of folded tape (see 3.5.1.1). The elastic cord shall be firmly clasped in the barrel lock when closed and shall pull smoothly through barrel lock when open. The pocket flaps shall be set 112 inch from the folded edge of pocket top (see pattem for placement). The cargo pockets and flaps shall close with a three (3) button (2) buttonhole closure per pocket. The buttons shall be sewn onto the outside ofthe pocket and the buttonholes shall be sewn onto the underside ofthe flap as indicated onpattems.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Lower Ie!!: Dockets and flaps. The trouser shall have two (2) lower leg bellows pockets with flaps (see pattern for placement). The pockets shall have a sew-in eyelet at the bottom of the bellow, as indicated onpattem (see 3.7.10). The pocket flaps shall be set 112 inch fi'om the folded edge of pocket top (see pattem for placement). The pockets shall close with one (I) piece ofloop fastener tape measuring I-inch wide by 3-112 inches long sewn to the underside of pocket flap and two (2) pieces of hook fastener tape measuring I-inch wide by I-inch long sewn to the outer side of pocket hem as indicated on pattem.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Leg bottom and hem. The trouser leg bottoms shall be hemmed and shall have a drawstring inserted through two (2) sewn-in eyelets or two (2) 112 inch horizontal straight cut buttonholes with reinforcement piece as indicated on patterns (see 3.7.9 and 3.11.1). The drawstling tape see (3.5 .1.1) shall overlap (cross) between holes when threaded through the hem casing. The drawstring shall be knotted at each end. The finished hem shall measure 7/8 (± 118) inch wide.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: Buttonholes. The buttonholes shall be eyelet-end tapered bar type worked over gimp for the fly, back hip welt pocket flaps, cargo pocket flaps and waistband with not less than four (4) tacking stitches at bar end catching the gimp ends (not counting the crossover stitch). The purling shall be on the outside surface. The cut lengths shall be 3/4 to 7/8 inch. The buttonholes shall be clean cut with the stitching securely caught in fabtic, possessing 52-56 stitches per inch, including tack. When buttonholes are used in lieu of sewn-in eyelets for the waistband and leg bottom hem drawsmngs they shall be 112 inch vertical straight cut for the waistband and 112 inch horizontal straight cut for the leg bottom hem.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.7.10 Eyelets. The sewn-in eyelets for the bellows pockets shall have a minimum of 16 stitches each with a 3/16 to 1/4 inch diameter finished opening. The width ofthe bight of stitching shall be not less than 1/16 inch. The eyelet stitching shall have at least four overlapping stitches with the purling on the outside (301 or 401 stitch type). When sewn-in eyelets are used for the waistband and leg bottom they shall measure 3/8 ± 1/8 inch in diameter.

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.7.11 Identification FR marker (Type II trouser only). The Type II trouser shall have a tape marker as specified in 3.5.1.2 on the left cargo pocket flap as worn (see pattern for placement). The tape marker shall finish I-inch (± 1/8) in length. The finished tape identification marker shall be box stitched as specified in Table V using 10- 14 stitches per inch. The thread shall be in accordance with the requirements for the Type II trouser (see 3.5.5.1).

elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.8 Labels. Each trouser shall have a size label and a combination identification/care label. The color of the labels shall be white or approximate the ground shade ofthe basic fab11c, and the printing shall be black. The inscription shall have a minimum font size of 8 points for identification/care label only. The font for the size label shall be 10 points. The inscription legibility, label, and label attachment shall last the expected life of the trouser.

Minor modifications are permitted where necessary to accommodate manufacture's processes and use of automatic equipment. These modifications shall not alter the design, serviceability, appearance or finished measurements. NOTE: When the 5-thread safety stitch is used for the inseam, contractor must adjust pattems for 3/8-inch gauge in lieu of 112 inch double needle seams. elements.label: text
elements.text: 3.11.1 Seams and stitching. All seams shall be consistent and exhibit a uniform appearance and confOlm to the ASTM D 6193 seam and stitch types listed in Table V. The backside of seams (inside garment) shall be flat with no protmding seam allowance to create irritation or discomfort. All material edges shall be clean finished, either, turned-in, turned-under or serged. All pocket flaps shall be serged prior to setting. Needle and bobbin thread tension shall be balanced such that neither is too tight nor too loose relative to each other. The seams for all outside visible stitching shall be sewn with 10-14 stitches per inch. Overedge or pre-hemming shall be 6-10 stitches per inch. As an alternate, the inseam may be safety stitched (5-thread) with 9 stitches per inch (min.) and top stitched with 10 -14 stitches per inch. Hook and loop tape shall be sewn with 8-12 stitches per inch. Buttons shall be attached with 16 stitches per button. The sewn eyelets for the bellows pockets shall have a minimum of 16 stitches.

elements.text: 3.11.1.1 Crotch intersection seaming and stitching. To reduce bulk when using a felled stitch seam at the crotch intersection, turn back the angled section ofthe seat patch (see pattern) and stitch down to the right side of the trouser back. See Table VI for bartack placement.
